correctness.rationale: Re-audited /workspace/repairs/2/RESULT.md. The digit series start with 1 and, at an internal irrational slope or a rational one-sided limit, contain infinitely many zeros and ones. Their roots are unique in (1,2); compact-uniform convergence and bracketing the strictly monotone root justify endpoint limits. The rational upper ceiling adds 1 to each cumulative count at positive multiples of q, so the two digit series differ by (1−t)t^q/(1−t^q). This gives both polynomials and the strict jump; the range cut argument with limiting bases 1 and 2 exhausts the complement of the closure. For rational slopes approaching an irrational, every finite prefix in both limit series eventually agrees with the irrational prefix, and q tends to infinity. At the left base B the right series has exact excess (1−1/B)B^(−q)/(1−B^(−q)). In the mean-value formula the derivative at the intermediate base converges by uniform summable domination and has strictly positive magnitude in the limit, giving the stated constant with B^q, not with the limiting base to that power. At scale n there are 1+Σ(q=2..n)φ(q) slope cells. The tail bound at every base b>1 passes to closure points along a fixed-prefix subsequence. Since the first digit is 1 the truncated series decreases at magnitude at least 1/4 on [1+ε,2]. This yields the claimed interval lengths and, via a countable exhaustion away from 1, Hausdorff dimension zero of C. The supplied bounded exact prefix/endpoint checks and numerical convergent test were inspected, not executed, and are not used to prove the limits.

evidence: Kwon proves slope continuity and strict increase with rational jumps, bounds the displacement of roots from a shared prefix using geometric tails (Lemma 2.5, Eq. (2)), and proves measure zero of the staircase range. His slope derivative theorem compares a change in base with a change in slope. Chi–Kwon's dimension-one statement concerns the wider class C_3; their conclusion for Sturmian numbers there is Lebesgue nullity. Anagnostopoulou–Jenkinson treat Farey concatenation and symbolic supports.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Null measure is not box dimension zero. Common-prefix stability is an ingredient of the explicit uniform cover, and is now credited. Symbolic supports and ordinary slope derivatives do not give the leading coefficient of the jump at a fixed rational, even as the rational varies toward an irrational.

originality.rationale: The frozen attribution of the algebraic endpoint and rational-gap description is materially incomplete: that part is covered by Kwon and fails originality as a distinct finding. The corrected manuscript explicitly presents it as prior work, adds the missing primary citation, and makes the denominator-normalized jump constant the main claim, with a quantitative prefix cover as a secondary consequence. This PASS applies to the repaired claim only. The cover combines known common-prefix stability with a simultaneous Farey-cell count; no priority is claimed for the basic stability or topology. The sharp coefficient for all rational approaches is distinct from the strongest inspected statements.

value.rationale: Given the known rational endpoints, the nontrivial quantitative question is their separation near an irrational base. The repaired result gives a strictly positive local calibration at the exponential scale for every reduced rational approach, with neither a continued-fraction restriction nor a rate hypothesis. It therefore answers a different question than algebraicity or a slope derivative and distinguishes the gap's scale from its coefficient. The explicit polynomial-size cover is useful supporting metric information but is not the sole basis for value.
